Following this process, four proponents were invited to participate in the second stage - a Limited Request for Tender (RFT) process. The objective of this procurement was to engage a suitably experienced head contractor for the design finalization and construction of Bank Street Park. The RFT was issued to the four shortlisted tenderers on February 28, 2025, and the closing date was extended twice, resulting in a final closing time of 3:00 pm on May 22, 2025. The RFT remained open to the market for a total period of 11 weeks and 6 days. The evaluation was conducted in accordance with the pre-approved Tender Evaluation Plan (TEP), which, among other matters, outlined the governance arrangements, evaluation criteria, and weightings. The TEP was endorsed by all Evaluation Committee members, as well as the Project Review Committee (PRC) and the Procurement and Probity Advisors.

The works include re-sheeting sections of 70km Trail within the Carrai, Willi Willi and Werrikimbe National Parks and in particular Coachwood and Carrai Roads. Gravel sheeting is required to improve traction and reduce slippage, after reshaping the carriageway surface. This process involves adding a layer of gravel, typically around 150mm thick, to the existing surface to create a more stable and less slippery riding surface. Gravel re-sheeting typically involves loosening the existing surface (e.g., with a tyning machine) to ensure proper bonding with the new gravel layer. A layer of new gravel is then spread evenly across the surface. Finally, the gravel is compacted to create a solid, stable surface. The works may also include clearing regrowth and vegetation, repairing trail surfaces, clearing drainage structures and culvert cleaning and repairs. This engagement will involve the provision of various plant and equipment items, each with qualified operators, under a wet hire arrangement. The equipment required includes: • D4/D5 Bulldozer with 6-way PAT blade • Grader • Roller • Water Cart • Rigid Truck • Posi Track • Moxy 30T Articulated Dump Truck • 1.7 Tonne Excavator • 14 Tonne Excavator Note: Plant may be required intermittently across different stages and must be available on an as-needed basis to meet program timelines.

Pathways to Community Living (PCLI) Stage 2 - Capital Consultants - Cost Manager

PCLI Stage 2 will deliver up to six separate supported housing facilities, each containing 10-20 single bedroom units which include facilities for independent daily living such as kitchen and laundry. Each facility will include staff support areas and shared communal spaces. The PCLI facilities will be single or two storey buildings of high quality residential nature and robust design. The buildings will be located within low/medium density residential areas or areas that are residential in character, to support community connection. PCLI facilities are not typical healthcare facilities and NSW Health has developed a draft Functional Design Brief to guide the design of PCLI facilities, which considers the specific requirements of PCLI consumers. These PCLI facilities will be delivered across up to six different sites. Two of these sites have been confirmed, two additional sites have been identified but not yet confirmed via Health governance, and two further sites have not yet been identified. The project comprises the core scope and two exercisable options: · Core scope: 20 PCLI beds across up to 2 sites · Option A: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option B: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option C: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site · Option D: 10 PCLI beds at 1 site.

Industry partners will co-design and co-deliver micro-credentials to ensure training is relevant and meets industry skills demands in the priority industries of the Western Parkland City. NETM Education and Training Providers with proven capacity and capability to deliver innovative, high-quality learning will be contracted to deliver NETM micro-credentials in collaboration with industry partners. To assess the efficacy and outcomes achieved by the NETM pilot, the Authority will be implementing an evaluation framework that sets out the source of outcomes metrics, evaluation instruments and data processes for NETM evaluation and reporting over the life of the pilot. Surveys of learners, employers, industry partners and education providers will be a key source of evaluation data to assess individual micro-credentials as well as the NETM process overall. This project aims to create a step-change in our capacity to enhance conservation outcomes for threatened species by assessing a suite of genomic tools that could provide managers with the critical information needed to rapidly decide on appropriate management actions. This project expects to bridge the gap between basic research and application by developing and applying new genomic tools to a real-world conservation case study. Expected outcomes include a framework for future integration of genomic approaches in adaptive conservation management. This should provide significant benefits, including increased accessibility to genomic tools that can rapidly provide the critical information needed to make informed conservation decisions.
